title: Mr. Ishibashi (the guard): a 3D model made the way Kuro, Aoi and Emi were
question: The first two sheets are ChatGPT pictures; every sheet after them is a render of the real rigged model, which you can turn in the live viewer next to Eric, Mio, Kuro, Aoi and Emi (link below). He is in the game now. Is the guard right?

media.caption: ChatGPT pictures. Your words: "can you also kick off the remaining staff and background characters in the new style". One chat in ChatGPT's image model (openai/gpt-5.4-image-2 on OpenRouter), as for Kuro, Aoi and Emi. Step 1 attached these two: the approved portrait and your Mio chibi.

ChatGPT pictures. Every take, in order, with your words as written: 1 "make a 3d chibi anime character in the style of the attached image" (a1, a2; a1 has his hands out and stands at an angle, so it went on), 2 "Simplify male character a LOT to match the detail level of the other chibi, with open eyes" (b1), 3 "Simpler head model, no glasses, no name plate, no shoulder patch" (c1: glasses, name plate, badge and patch gone; the thin moustache became a thick one), then your angle prompt with "he" and "his" (d1). Head share in d1: 0.41 (Eric 0.46, Kuro 0.41, Aoi 0.40, Emi 0.43), so no head-size follow-up. 5 takes, $1.24.
Renders of the real model from here on. Meshy image-to-3D from d1 with Kuro's settings: smart topology (meshy-t2), 1,050 polygons, A-pose, no texture, 5 credits. Meshy's previews; first roll, kept.

The face-first UV unwrap before the texture pass (Aoi's uv_bl.py): the front of the face as one piece at 3 times the detail of the rest (68 polygons, red; his eyes are modelled as separate sunken pieces, so they are added to the face's piece (the script's new also= option) and painted with it). Then Meshy retexture on that mesh, styled from d1, keep the UVs, lighting removed, no PBR, 10 credits. Right: the texture Meshy painted.
The textured model: front, three-quarter (the left side of the image turned to us), side, back, the other three-quarter, face. Same camera and light as Kuro's, Aoi's and Emi's rounds.

From below the chin in the texture's own colours: no black marks on the skin (cheek_fix.py finds no dark texels on the skin under his jaw). There are grey-blue streaks along the underside of his moustache and a pale blue patch under his chin, both only visible from below; the game's camera looks down on him, so the texture is in the game as Meshy painted it. Say if they should be repainted.

Head share on the models (straight-on, flat colour, rest pose, each figure at the same height): Eric 0.46, Kuro 0.41, Aoi 0.40, Emi 0.43, the guard 0.46 (0.41 in the picture). Hands, counted from the rig's hand bones: 0.139 of his height, against Eric 0.107, Mio 0.105, Kenji 0.102, Mori 0.093. So, as for Aoi, the game scales his two hand bones to 0.75 when he loads (0.104, Eric's size); the live viewer shows them as Meshy made them.
Mr. Ishibashi (the guard) beside the in-game Eric and Mio and Kuro (the same render script and camera), front and three-quarter.

Meshy auto-rig at 1.1 m, 5 credits, and Meshy's Chair_Sit_Idle_F for his chair at the gate desk, 3 credits. Stills from the live viewer (rest, idle, walk, walk from the side); the idle and walk are the game's. Meshy credits for the guard: 23 (shape 5, texture 10, rig 5, sit 3); balance 297 after him.
In the game (day 1, 1366x860, test mode): the gate from above, and the guard seated at his desk as Eric comes up to it, and at "nine o'clock" (the clock emote over him).
